I opened the page, and the quoted words appear on it word for word. They are in Pichai's own signed section, so I read this as a pass.

**Page check.** The page is Google's 11 December 2024 post "Introducing Gemini 2.0: our new AI model for the agentic era". It has three authors: Pichai, Demis Hassabis and Koray Kavukcuoglu. The sentence sits inside the section headed "A note from Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai:", which ends "-Sundar". So these are Pichai's own words, not a news report or part of the Hassabis and Kavukcuoglu section that follows. The sentence just before it gives the context: "we're bringing the advanced reasoning capabilities of Gemini 2.0 to AI Overviews to tackle more complex topics and multi-step questions, including advanced math equations, multimodal queries and coding."

**Admission rule:**
1. **Role:** On 11 December 2024 he was chief executive of Google (from 2015) and Alphabet (from 2019). Google builds the Gemini models and its own AI chips, so the role qualifies.
2. **Forward-looking and about AI:** It says an AI feature, Gemini 2.0 reasoning in AI Overviews, will roll out more broadly. That is a claim about where an AI system will be deployed, not a business or hardware forecast. It isn't framed as a hypothetical.
3. **Date:** "Early next year" means early 2025. Under ruled reading 1, that sets the due date to 31 March 2025.
4. **Primary source:** It is his own signed words.

**Already recorded?** No. None of his recorded files covers this claim. The nearest ones are different claims: "search will evolve significantly in 2025" (29 October 2024) and "Gemini 2.5 to Search this week" (20 May 2025).

**For whoever writes the test:** "more broadly" names no scale, so the test may only be able to check that a wider release happened by 31 March 2025. That affects scoring, not whether the claim gets in.
